title: Uniform and Compass
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, Ulyana Okafor carries a diplomatic code pouch aboard the last evacuation ship bound for neutral ports, convinced that ordinary people can outlast history by staying small. But a census taker at the harbor records his name, his lineage, and one answer too many, marking him and his family for detention. As the ship's departure slips from days to hours, Ulyana discovers the code he carries is worth more than money—it is leverage, and men will kill for it. In the end, he trades the code to a corrupt port official for two berths instead of three, gives his own place to his sister's son, and escapes the republic as someone else entirely—alive, unseen, and forever complicit in the arithmetic of survival.
about_author: Ivo Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging passenger manifests from collapsed states. Uniform and Compass is his second novel, drawn from an unsigned letter found sewn into a life vest.

chapters.title: The Question That Wasn't on the Form
chapters.summary: Ulyana Okafor, a minor clerk turned courier, waits in the frozen queue at Vessa Harbor while a census taker works the line. Asked his mother's maiden name—a question no form requires—he answers before thinking. POV: Ulyana. Beat: quiet dread taking root beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Pouch, A Promise, A Republic
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: how Ulyana inherited the courier duty from his dying mentor Tomas, who called it 'a favor no one survives owing.' The sealed code pouch sleeps under his coat. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the weight of inheritance disguised as errand.

chapters.title: Sister of Salt and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Marisol, who keeps the family's smuggling accounts, to arrange passage for their household. She reads the harbor notices and tells him his name appeared on yesterday's census list. POV: Marisol. Beat: fear sharpened into practical fury.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counts Berths
chapters.summary: Nephew Denny, eleven, inventories what each family member can carry aboard, treating escape like a game. Ulyana watches him and cannot speak. POV: Ulyana. Beat: tenderness curdling into dread—the list has too many names.

chapters.title: Men in Good Coats
chapters.summary: Two officials visit Ulyana's lodging, courteous, asking about 'documents in transit.' They know the pouch exists; they don't know he knows. He lies well for the first time in his life. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the intoxicating and terrifying discovery that lying is a skill.

chapters.title: What the Census Taker Keeps
chapters.summary: The census taker, Herr Brandt, is revealed in his own POV: a tired functionary who sells names to whichever faction pays, keeping duplicates as insurance. Ulyana's entry sits in his third ledger. POV: Brandt. Beat: banality of betrayal.

chapters.title: Marisol's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marisol lays out the numbers: four family members, two berths she can secure, three days. She proposes leaving the eldest aunt behind; Ulyana refuses; the argument goes somewhere unforgivable. POV: Marisol. Beat: love weaponized into triage.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Price
chapters.summary: Ulyana approaches the harbormaster, Grieves, who names an obscene price in hard currency—and then, seeing the pouch's seal, changes his price to the contents themselves. POV: Ulyana. Beat: hope arriving wearing a predator's face.

chapters.title: Tomas's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Searching Tomas's effects for a way to open or counterfeit the code, Ulyana finds a letter: the pouch contains not orders but evidence—names of officials who sold the republic's defense plans. It is a bomb made of paper. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the mission was never what he thought.

chapters.title: Brandt Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Brandt appears at Marisol's door, offering to erase the family's census record—for the pouch. He speaks of it like a man discussing weather. Ulyana stalls. POV: alternating Ulyana/Brandt. Beat: two liars circling, both aware.

chapters.title: Denny Runs
chapters.summary: Frightened by overheard arguments, Denny tries to stow away on the ship early and is caught by dock police. Ulyana buys his release with the last of Marisol's hidden currency. POV: Denny. Beat: childhood ending mid-sentence.

chapters.title: The Aunt Who Refuses
chapters.summary: Aunt Vesna, matriarch, announces she will not board any ship; her life, her grave, her choice. Her dignity reframes the berth question no one wanted to say aloud. POV: Marisol. Beat: grief masquerading as relief, shame following.

chapters.title: Grieves Tightens the Screw
chapters.summary: The harbormaster moves departure up twelve hours—another buyer has offered more. He gives Ulyana until dawn. Meanwhile soldiers begin door-to-door searches near the docks. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the walls closing with bureaucratic politeness.

chapters.title: A Forged Compass
chapters.summary: Marisol forges transit papers using her ledger skills; Ulyana practices being 'Ivo Renner,' a grain merchant. The disguise fits disturbingly well—he likes the man he's pretending to be. POV: Ulyana. Beat: identity as costume, and its seduction.

chapters.title: The Third Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana breaks into Brandt's office to steal the family's census page and finds all three ledgers—leverage over half the port's officials. He takes only his own page, and hates himself for the restraint. POV: Ulyana. Beat: justice within reach, declined.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: Marisol's contact sells their meeting time to Grieves' rival. Ambushed, Marisol is detained; Ulyana escapes with the pouch because she shoved him into a fish cellar first. POV: Marisol. Beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: Two Berths, Three Names
chapters.summary: With Marisol in custody, the math collapses: Ulyana and Denny can board, but only if he surrenders the pouch to Grieves tonight. He negotiates Marisol's release into the bargain—two berths, three lives, one code. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the terrible clarity of the deal.

chapters.title: What the Code Was Worth
chapters.summary: Ulyana delivers the pouch; Grieves opens it, reads, and goes pale—the names include Grieves' own patrons. Realizing its true value, Grieves tries to renege and keep everything. POV: Grieves. Beat: greed outrunning prudence.

chapters.title: The Dock at Dawn
chapters.summary: Climax: Ulyana, having memorized key pages before surrendering, threatens to distribute copies unless all three walk aboard. Soldiers arrive for Brandt's ledgers; chaos erupts on the pier. Marisol frees herself in the crush. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the moment survival stops being passive.

chapters.title: Gangway
chapters.summary: Amid smoke and shouting, Ulyana forces Grieves at improvised leverage to honor the bargain. Vesna, changed mind unknown, is already aboard—she boarded at night, choosing life after all. The whistle blows. POV: Ulyana. Beat: exhalation after drowning.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: At sea, the family counts itself: four alive, one nation dead. Denny asks what Ulyana gave up; Ulyana says 'paper.' Marisol, who saw his face during the trade, says nothing. POV: Denny. Beat: inheritance passing quietly to the next generation.

chapters.title: The Man Named Renner
chapters.summary: Epilogue, neutral port, spring: Ulyana lives under his forged name, sends anonymous copies of the surviving code pages to foreign newspapers—justice outside any law. The last line reveals he kept one page: Tomas's letter. POV: Ulyana. Beat: peace purchased, never clean.
